text:
maria: quick heads-up — after the kernel reorder landed yesterday I’m seeing a noticeable uptick in KV fragmentation on p3-small pools. spike correlates with larger workspace allocations from the fused-attn matmul path.

josh: ugh. any OOMs?

maria: two hard OOMs in prod-canary 10:42–10:58. p95 token latency also crept ~8%. paste of allocator log: 
```
[10:43:12] allocator: alloc(workspace=1.2GB) -> slab=2048KB align=4096 id=0x7f
[10:43:12] kv_cache: insert(key=conv-XXXX, size=512KB) -> slabfrag=0.63
[10:44:01] allocator: alloc(workspace=1.8GB) -> slab=2048KB align=4096 id=0x8a
[10:44:01] OOM: request_id=... kernel=matmul_fused
[10:44:02] evictor: scanned=1200 entries, reclaimed=3MB
```
Link to flamegraph: https://internal-redwood/fg/3476543210

ari: interesting — alignment at 4k + large workspace peaks could cause many partially filled slabs. those 512KB KV entries with fragmentation=0.63 are expensive.

sam: are we sure it's the kernel selection and not a regression in prefill heuristics? recent commits touched both.

maria: agreed both changed. timeline: kernel reorder -> bigger temp buffers -> allocator rounds up -> prefill still writes full-size entries -> fragmentation. perf regressions align to kernel change by timestamps.

josh: rough mitigation options: 1) emergency: lower workspace caps per-request (soft cap) 2) medium: adaptive per-request soft cap based on seq-length histogram 3) longer: compaction pass that coalesces small KV slots during low-qps windows.

ari: I sketched a compaction idea last week — run a background compactor on otherwise idle GPU streams that tries to coalesce same-size adjacent slots by memcpy+pointer-fixups. cost is a short pause but we can schedule when driver queue depth is low.

maria: that seems promising. sketch of adaptive cap config I want to try (sampled on 1% of requests):
```
{"kv_soft_cap_mb": "adaptive",
 "histogram_window_minutes": "15",
 "quantiles": ["50","90","99"],
 "cap_formula": "base + factor * q90_seq_len",
 "min_cap_mb": "128",
 "max_cap_mb": "2048"
}
```

josh: nice. we should also tweak prefill threshold: if seq_len > q99 then prefer decode-path-only (no prefill write) to avoid creating big KV entries.

sam: worry: disabling prefill for long seqs could increase p99 latency for those requests. need to simulate end-to-end.

maria: plan:
- run mem-sculptor sim with current allocation traces to estimate frag_ratio change (target <0.25)
- bench adaptive soft caps vs static caps (measure tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, kv_frag_ratio)
- implement lightweight compaction prototype behind feature flag (canary 1%)
- add metrics: kv_frag_ratio, kv_coalesces, compactor_pauses_ms, per_request_workspace_mb

ari: I’ll open a PR for the compactor prototype (WIP) and add perf microbench. tagging @josh for allocator-side knobs.

josh: I’ll add the soft-cap sampler + histogram collector to runtime, and a canary flag. also wired a Prom alert: kv_frag_ratio > 0.4 -> paging.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/canary-compact-v1 -> 2026-11-02T18:00Z (staged 1%) :rocket:

sam: tiny ask — add an e2e with a mix of short/long sequences (80/20) so we catch latency regressions early.

maria: will do. next sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. action items captured in the thread. :white_check_mark:

ari: one more thought — kernel selection hinting: when choosing the fused path we can annotate expected temporary workspace and have the router pick a node with spare contiguous slab range. this reduces co-location of big allocations on same GPU. probably low-effort and high-impact.

josh: good call. router > allocator hints sounds clean — I’ll prototype a slot-reservation API (opt-in).

maria: thanks all. saving logs to ticket RED-2983 and adding perf graphs.

sam: thanks — great triage. :thumbsup:
